stem: A printer is available at 09:00. Setup takes 10 minutes; three batches then take 15 minutes each. A mandatory 10-minute check follows batch two and precedes batch three. After setup, an independent clerk can prepare a cover sheet in 25 minutes while printing continues. A final 5-minute assembly requires all batches and the cover sheet; nothing else can overlap. When is the earliest complete packet ready?
explanation: The printer/check path finishes at 09:00+10+15+15+10+15=10:05. The cover sheet starts after setup at 09:10 and finishes at 09:35, so it does not extend that path. Assembly waits for both and ends at 10:10. Omitting assembly gives 10:05; serialising the independent cover-sheet work gives 10:35; overlapping the required check with batch three violates precedence.

stem: Under a local ledger rule, receipts count on receipt date and refunds on refund date. A bank deposit includes receipts net of refunds actually paid and any money retained as the cash float. On 31 March, receipts are PHP 9000; a PHP 400 refund for a February receipt is paid; a PHP 600 refund for a March receipt is authorised but not paid until April. PHP 500 from today's net cash is retained as the float, not an expense. Which pair is correct for March net recorded activity and today's bank deposit?

choices.text: PHP 8600 net activity; PHP 8600 bank deposit
PHP 8600 net activity; PHP 8100 bank deposit
PHP 8000 net activity; PHP 7500 bank deposit
PHP 8100 net activity; PHP 8100 bank deposit

explanation: March activity includes 9000 receipts less the 400 refund paid in March: 8600. The April payment is excluded by the supplied date rule. Keeping a 500 float does not reduce activity but does reduce the deposit to 8100. The alternatives respectively book the April refund early, treat a transfer as an expense, or overlook retained cash.
